extraction.Name: George Colhoff
extraction.Refused/Protested: he applied for a patent to the allotment on his north quarter, and got it in 1911, then on the south quarter, he took what is called a forced patent, being told by the Indian Agency that it would have to be taxed at any rate, so he, also, accepted the patent to the allotment on his south quarter
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged his 320 acres for about $3000; finally lost the allotment
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: using some of this money for taxes, and some for chattels; that he finally lost the allotment, on account of prices in cattle dropping and some of his cattle died
extraction.Fee Patent Date: 1911 (north quarter); south quarter date not stated
extraction.Occupation/Income: chief income is from farming his wife's allotment and laboring for other people
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; pretty good health; has a wife and six minor children to support; health of wife and children is not very good, all being bothered with heart trouble; has never received any help from the County or United States Government; affidavit sworn November 13, 1928; allotment consisted of 320 acres (north quarter and south quarter)
